rows.title: Radisson Riviera Panama
rows.body:
Beachfront, Panama, CALA, Conversion, Pacific coast, Extended stay

Chamé, Panamá Oeste, Panama (~1 hour west of Panama City)

Conversion / repositioning · ~92 rooms · beach resort with in-room kitchens

Radisson Riviera Panama debuted in 2025 on Panama's Pacific coast in the Playa Caracol / Punta Chamé area. Press and developer materials describe a beachfront Radisson (not Radisson Blu) with kitchens in guest rooms, dining, rooftop terrace, gym, spa, and pools—aimed at families and drive-out leisure from Panama City. The project is reported at roughly US$19 million, developed with Choice Hotels and Grupo Los Pueblos following renovation of the former Surfside Hotel.

The core Radisson flag fits an "affordable luxury" coastal product under Choice distribution—distinct from upper-tier Blu or lifestyle sub-brands. For owners, it shows how the network can place mainstream Radisson in a master-planned beach community with local development partners and cited job creation (developer materials reference 250+ direct and indirect jobs).

CALA proof point for conversion-led beach growth: Radisson can enter secondary Pacific markets via renovation and JV structures, not only urban new-build prototypes. Treat occupancy and returns as diligence items—this card summarizes public positioning only.

https://www.choicehotels.com/es-mx/panama/panama/radisson-hotels/pn018
rows.caseSummaryOverview: Chamé / Playa Caracol: core Radisson (not Blu or RED) beach resort on Panama's Pacific coast—publicly described as a ~92-room conversion after renovation of the former Surfside Hotel, with roughly US$19 million investment and Choice Hotels × Grupo Los Pueblos development.
rows.caseSummaryOwnerObjective: Capture drive-out leisure and weekend demand from Panama City while offering kitchen-equipped rooms and full-service amenities for families and longer stays—not a CBD gateway play.
rows.caseSummaryBrandRelevance: Useful when the owner story is "coastal conversion or independent resort asset → Choice distribution + recognizable Radisson flag" without moving to Blu, Collection, or lifestyle sub-brands.
rows.caseSummaryInterpretation: Compare conversion CapEx, PIP timing, and beach-season ramp versus the press headline—public sourcing is real; RevPAR, fees, and operator readiness remain deal-specific.
rows.caseSummaryTags: Panama, CALA, Beachfront, Conversion, Pacific coast, Extended stay

rows.title: Radisson Puebla Angelópolis
rows.body:
Urban upscale, Mexico, CALA, Meetings, Mixed-use corridor

Puebla, Puebla, Mexico (Angelópolis district)

New-build / greenfield · 80 rooms · meetings + spa + rooftop F&B

Choice Hotels CALA inaugurated Radisson Puebla Angelópolis on 14 October 2024 in Puebla's Angelópolis corridor, minutes from the historic center. The property is described as an 80-room Radisson with Mexican–international restaurant, rooftop bar, spa, fitness center, and three meeting rooms for up to ~215 guests. Reported investment: MXN 365 million; ~40 direct and ~100 indirect jobs.

Core Radisson strengthens Choice's multi-brand stack in a secondary city (alongside Comfort Inn and Sleep Inn in the same market). The story is urban commercial + cultural tourism—not a resort sub-brand—so it reads as full-service Radisson for business and leisure compression.

Use for CALA urban greenfield: Radisson as a meetings-capable upscale box in growing Mexican cities. Verify fee stack, comp set, and ramp vs. Angelópolis supply before underwriting.

https://www.choicehotels.com/en-mx/mexico/puebla/radisson-hotels/mxpue
rows.caseSummaryOverview: October 2024 opening: 80-room Radisson Puebla Angelópolis in Puebla's Angelópolis district (MXN 365 million investment)—meetings capacity to ~215 guests, spa, rooftop bar, and Mexican–international dining under Choice Hotels CALA.
rows.caseSummaryOwnerObjective: Win urban commercial, meetings, and cultural-tourism demand in a growing secondary city with a full-service Radisson box and portfolio loyalty retail—not a resort or lifestyle prototype.
rows.caseSummaryBrandRelevance: Illustrates core Radisson in Mexico as an upscale urban greenfield alongside sibling Choice brands (Comfort Inn, Sleep Inn) in the same market—distinct from Radisson Blu or Collection positioning.
rows.caseSummaryInterpretation: Validate fee economics, Angelópolis comp-set supply, and ramp assumptions before treating the inauguration as performance proof—public investment and job figures are positioning, not audited hotel results.
rows.caseSummaryTags: Mexico, CALA, Urban upscale, Meetings, Greenfield, Angelópolis

rows.title: Radisson San Luis Potosí, Aeropuerto
rows.body:
Airport, Mexico, CALA, Industrial corridor, Business travel

Soledad de Graciano Sánchez / San Luis Potosí, Mexico (near Ponciano Arriaga Airport)

Airport-oriented full-service · 65 rooms · restaurant, gym, business center

The Radisson San Luis Potosí, Aeropuerto held its official opening on 11 February 2025 in Rancho Nuevo, Soledad—positioned as the closest branded option to Ponciano Arriaga International Airport and ~25 minutes from the industrial zone. Press cites MXN 120+ million investment, 65 rooms, 40 direct jobs, plus restaurant, gym, and business facilities. Choice's Mexico & Central America leadership participated in the inauguration.

This is classic Radisson (not Blu): airport capture, corporate and government demand, and industrial adjacency—lower glamour than beach or lifestyle flags but strong for contract and transient mix narratives in CALA.

Owner lens: airport Radisson as infrastructure play—evaluate capture from O&D vs. crew, parking/shuttle economics, and dual-brand overlap if another Radisson already serves the metro. Public sources frame it as Choice CALA's second Radisson in the San Luis market.

https://www.choicehotels.com/en-mx/mexico/san-luis-potosi/radisson-hotels/slpap
rows.caseSummaryOverview: February 2025 opening: Radisson San Luis Potosí, Aeropuerto in Rancho Nuevo, Soledad—65 rooms, MXN 120+ million investment, positioned as the nearest branded full-service option to Ponciano Arriaga International Airport and ~25 minutes from the industrial zone.
rows.caseSummaryOwnerObjective: Serve airline, corporate, government, and industrial travelers with airport proximity, restaurant, gym, and business-center infrastructure—transient and contract mix over leisure design narrative.
rows.caseSummaryBrandRelevance: Classic core Radisson under Choice CALA for airport and industrial corridors—not RED, Blu, or Collection—when distribution and recognizable full-service standards matter more than lifestyle storytelling.
rows.caseSummaryInterpretation: Model O&D versus crew demand, shuttle and parking economics, and any second Radisson in the metro before underwriting—airport flags win on access and capture, not on resort rate ceiling.
rows.caseSummaryTags: Mexico, CALA, Airport, Industrial corridor, Business travel, San Luis Potosí
